title: Schedule of Credit Bases and Ceilings under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes
content:
Each of the six Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes works the credit for a traded piece out on one published basis, at one published share of that basis, and issues no more than one published ceiling against one traded piece. The schedule below is the programme office's statement of those figures. The basis is one of four: the price the piece originally sold for, its current appraised value, its certified laboratory value, or the published scrap rate for its metal.

## Schedule

| Programme | Basis the credit is worked out on | Share of the original selling price | Share of the current appraised value | Largest credit for one traded piece (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Belrose Standard Trade-In | current appraised value | 50 percent | 40 percent | 4999 |
| Diamond Trade-Up Guarantee | price originally sold for | 100 percent | 60 percent | 24999 |
| Bridal Upgrade Guarantee | price originally sold for | 100 percent | 65 percent | 39999 |
| Lifetime Diamond Upgrade Guarantee | price originally sold for | 100 percent | 70 percent | 74999 |
| Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege | certified laboratory value | 110 percent | 75 percent | 199999 |
| Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme | current appraised value | 0 percent | 55 percent | 149999 |

## What is valued: stone alone or stone with mounting

| Programme | Credit given for the stone alone | Mounting credited alongside the stone |
|---|---|---|
| Belrose Standard Trade-In | no | yes |
| Diamond Trade-Up Guarantee | yes | no |
| Bridal Upgrade Guarantee | yes | no |
| Lifetime Diamond Upgrade Guarantee | yes | no |
| Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege | no | yes |
| Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme | no | yes |

## Metal taken as scrap

Where a programme pays for metal taken as scrap, it pays the published share of the metal's spot price: 72 percent under the Belrose Standard Trade-In and 80 percent under the Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme. The four guarantee programmes publish a scrap share of 0 percent, which is to say that they do not take metal as scrap at all.

## Footnotes to the schedule

1. The two shares are published side by side because each programme has one of each; which of them the programme's basis calls on is a matter for the rule that works the credit out, and the schedule fixes only the figures.
2. The largest credit is a ceiling on what is issued against one traded piece, not a ceiling on what a customer may hold in total across several registrations.
3. A share of 110 percent, as the Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege publishes for the original selling price, means the figure exceeds the price by a tenth; a share of 0 percent, as the Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme publishes for the original selling price, means that basis yields nothing under that programme.
